newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-HAKKINEN COOL AFTER CLOCKING FASTEST PRACTICE TIME.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HAKKINEN COOL AFTER CLOCKING FASTEST PRACTICE TIME.

text.p: Mika Hakkinen stayed cool and played down his prospects of claiming the first Formula One victory of his career on Friday after topping the practice times in his McLaren for Sunday's British Grand Prix.

The 28-year-old Finn clocked a best time of one minute 22.935 seconds, but less than a second separated him from sixth-placed Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan -- with world championship-leading German Michael Schumacher seventh in his Ferrari.

"It is very competitive and, naturally, I am very pleased with my time," he said. "The performance of the car was fantastic, but I have reminded myself that it is only free practice and it does not really matter. So, I intend to stay cool."

This weekend, Hakkinen is taking part in his 88th Grand Prix and recognises he is under pressure following the escalation of paddock rumours that either he, or his British McLaren team-mate David Coulthard, will be replaced in the team next year.

Hakkinen is not worried. "I don't feel I have to win a race in order to keep my place in the team, but it would be very nice if I could. But you can never count on anything in Formula One. You just never know what is going to happen.

"At the moment, I feel very comfortable in my car and very confident. I am enjoying racing this car and I am hoping to do well. I feel I know it well now. To drive a Grand Prix car these days is very complicated and not at all easy.

"It is not a case of sitting down and using the brakes and the accelerator and sometimes changing gear while you are steering. It is much more than that. There are so many instruments and so many things to think about all the time."

Hakkinen acknowledged that Mercedes-Benz would expect success after spending a great deal of money on engine development. But, he said, that did not mean that they had to change the team or the drivers.
"We feel good and confident, so we will carry on doing our best -- and I like to think we can win here."
For Hakkinen, and McLaren, his strong practice showing was a welcome indication that the Mercedes-Benz powered team could be a force in Sunday's 60-lap race.

On a cool day with a slight breeze, Hakkinen was just three- tenths of a second ahead of Canadian Jacques Villeneuve in the leading Williams, but the Renault-powered British team are expected to improve in response as they seek to score their 100th victory.
Villeneuve's Williams team-mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany was third-fastest ahead of Briton Johnny Herbert in a Sauber and Frenchman Jean Alesi in a Benetton.

World champion Damon Hill of Britain languished in 20th place in his Arrows on the the day after his team chief Tom Walkinshaw had warned him to improve his performance and show the talent that took him to the title last year.
